blocks.body: A license is permission to be the control operator of an amateur station, inside the rules. It is not permission to use a transmitter for any purpose you like. Band edges from Foundations Lab 04 still apply. This page is a teaching summary, not the rule book.
Open the core reference when a situation is unclear. That is normal.

config.doneText: The license makes you responsible for what the station transmits. Access to the radio is not the same thing as permission to transmit.

scenes.prompt: A friend who is not licensed wants to borrow your radio for the afternoon and transmit while you are gone.

choices.label: Lend the radio. Your license covers the equipment.
choices.why: The license belongs to the operator, not to the radio as a free pass. Someone has to be the control operator, at the control point, for the transmissions.

choices.label: Do not let the radio transmit unless a licensed control operator is there and responsible.
choices.why: You can own the radio and still not be the control operator of a contact that happens while you are away. The friend needs to be licensed, or you need to be the control operator.

choices.label: Tell the friend to use your call sign so the station is identified.
choices.why: Saying your call sign does not make an unlicensed person the control operator.

scenes.prompt: Someone asks you to play recorded music over the amateur station for a neighborhood event.

choices.label: Play it. A license means the frequency is yours to program.
choices.why: Amateur transmissions are not a broadcast service. Music for an audience is not the purpose of the station.

choices.label: Decline. Playing music for an audience is not an amateur communication.
choices.why: The station is for amateur communications. A music broadcast is a different service. The license does not convert the radio into a broadcast transmitter.

choices.label: Play it if you identify every 10 minutes.
choices.why: Identification makes a transmission attributable. It does not make a prohibited transmission allowed.

scenes.prompt: A neighbor offers to pay you to pass messages on the amateur radio for a delivery business.

choices.label: Accept. Emergency and business messages are the same if you identify.
choices.why: Getting paid to carry communications is not an amateur transmission. Identification does not change that.

choices.label: Decline the paid communications.
choices.why: Amateur operation is not a hired message service. A real emergency is a different situation from a delivery contract.

choices.label: Accept if the neighbor is also licensed.
choices.why: Two licenses do not turn the contact into a paid communications service.

scenes.prompt: A family member wants to say hello, briefly, to a friend on your station.

choices.label: Hand over the radio and leave. They only need a minute.
choices.why: An unlicensed person can speak only while a control operator is in charge of the station.

choices.label: Stay as the control operator, allow the brief hello if the content is otherwise permitted, and identify the station.
choices.why: A third party may speak under the control operator. You remain responsible. You identify the station. The hello is not a program and not a paid message.

choices.label: Refuse every third-party word. Only the licensee may speak.
choices.why: A brief permitted message for another person is a normal amateur use when the control operator is present.

blocks.body: During a contact, identify the station often enough that a listener can tell who is transmitting. This clock uses a 10-minute gap and an identification at the end.
Two more decisions, then the edge of the 2-meter allocation. A signal has width. The center frequency is not the whole emission.

config.doneText: A test is still your transmission. A picnic does not require a new license, and it does not erase the identification rule.

scenes.prompt: You want to test the transmitter on the air.

choices.label: Key the radio and say nothing, so you do not clutter the frequency.
choices.why: A test is a transmission. Listen first, keep it short, and identify. A silent key-up is still you.

choices.label: Listen first, keep the test short, identify, and use only enough power to make the test.
choices.why: The legal maximum is a ceiling. The operating habit is the lowest power that does the job. A dummy load, in the next labs, keeps a bench test from radiating.

choices.label: Use the highest power the radio offers so the test is obvious.
choices.why: More power is not a better test. It is more likely to bother another station.

scenes.prompt: You take the same radio from home to a park in the United States.

choices.label: You need a new license for the new location before you can transmit.
choices.why: The operator license travels with you. A change of mailing address is a database duty. It is not a new license for each picnic.

choices.label: You may operate under the same license, still as the control operator, and you still identify.
choices.why: The privilege is yours. The control point is wherever you are actually controlling the station. Identification and the band limits come with you.

choices.label: Leave the call sign at home because the radio is now portable.
choices.why: The call sign identifies the station wherever it is operating.

blocks.prompt: Why does having access to a transmitter not give you permission to use it however you want?
blocks.reference: The license authorizes you to be a control operator inside the amateur service. It does not make the transmitter a broadcast station, a hired circuit, or a radio anyone can use in your absence. You choose the frequency, the power, the content, and the identification. Access to the hardware is only the start of that responsibility.
blocks.unsure: Go back to the four situations. In each one the radio could physically transmit. The license still said no, or it said yes only with you in control.

blocks.body: RADIO LAB PRACTICE. These questions are about the decisions you just made. They are not official exam questions, and a miss is not a failed license.

blocks.label: RADIO LAB PRACTICE
blocks.notice: Original practice about the decisions you just made. Not official exam questions. A miss is a review topic, not a failed license.

questions.stem: Which activity fits the amateur service in this lab?
choices: Selling airtime for a neighborhood music show
A personal contact, including emergency communications, under the control operator
questions.why: The service is for amateur communications, including emergencies and training. It is not a broadcast or a hired circuit.

questions.stem: Your license grant is still inside its term. What is a fair statement from this lab?
choices: The usual term is 10 years, and the two-year grace period is not permission to transmit
The license expires every year and the radio must stay at the original address
A grace period is an extra two years of on-air privileges
questions.why: The teaching point is a 10-year term. During the grace period you may renew without retesting, and you do not transmit as if the license were still active.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for a transmission from your station?
choices: Whoever is holding the microphone, licensed or not
questions.why: The control operator is responsible and must be in control. Lending the radio does not move that duty onto an unlicensed friend.

questions.stem: During a long contact, when does this lab ask you to identify?
choices: Only the first time you turn the radio on that day
Often enough to stay inside a 10-minute gap, and again at the end
Only if another station asks for your name
questions.why: The timeline refused a gap longer than 10 minutes and required an identification at the end.

questions.stem: You can legally use more power than the contact needs. What should you do?
choices: Use the lowest power that completes the contact
Use the legal maximum so the signal is as strong as the rules allow
Sit on the band edge, because the center frequency is all that counts
questions.why: The maximum is a ceiling. The habit is the minimum power that works. The emission also has width, so the edge of the signal has to stay inside the allocation.

questions.stem: A family member wants to say a brief hello on your station. What keeps that inside this lab's rule?
choices: You leave, and they use your call sign
You stay as control operator, the hello is otherwise permitted, and you identify
They pay for the batteries, so the message is authorized
questions.why: Third-party speech is possible with the control operator present. Payment and an absent licensee take it outside the permission you practiced.

blocks.body: First day with the license. You are at a trailhead with your own radio. Make the operating decisions. This does not finish Technician Core or make you exam-ready.

config.doneText: You kept the control operator duty, refused the paid messages, and identified. That is a usable first day, not the whole license.

scenes.prompt: Before you call, a hiker offers you cash to send delivery updates on the radio.

choices.label: Decline.
choices.why: Paid communications are not the contact you came to make.

choices.label: Accept if you identify first.
choices.why: Identification does not authorize communications for hire.

scenes.prompt: You make a contact. It runs long.

choices.label: Identify during the contact and at the end.
choices.why: The call sign has to stay attached to the transmission.

choices.label: Skip the call sign because the other station already knows you.
choices.why: Familiarity is not identification.

scenes.prompt: Your sibling wants to say hello to the other station.

choices.label: You stay at the radio as control operator and allow the brief hello.
choices.why: You remain responsible. The sibling is not the control operator.

choices.label: You walk to the overlook and leave them the microphone.
choices.why: The control operator has to be in control of the station.
